Case Name: Register AgentCard and query it (with mTLS client identity)
Precondition: Registry Center deployed via Helm with mTLS client certificate configured
Steps:
1. Submit the signed AgentCard with the configured client certificate via POST /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards
2. Query the Agent via GET /rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards/{org}/{name}
Expected Result:
1. Registration succeeds with a success status returned
2. The query returns fields consistent with the submitted content
Notes: Generate the AgentCard signature (JWS RS256) first

Precondition: Registry Center deployed; LLM endpoint available or mock enabled
Steps:
1. Publish at least two AgentCards with different capabilities to the Registry Center
2. Submit a natural-language task description matching that capability to invoke the semantic search API
Expected Result:
1. Search results are ranked by relevance
2. The returned AgentCard capabilities match the task description (deterministic assertions on LLM output: status code/structure/ranking fields)
Notes: With USE_MOCK_LLM=true, assert structure rather than text

Case Name: Generate a workflow from intent and execute the end-to-end closed loop
Precondition: Orchestration Center and Registry Center deployed; sample agents started; login state acquired
Steps:
1. Log in to the Orchestration Center to get a session
2. Submit a natural-language intent to the generation API to obtain a PSOP
3. Execute the PSOP and subscribe to the SSE event stream
4. Observe the execution status and event sequence
Expected Result:
1. PSOP is generated successfully with a valid structure (acyclic DAG, correct context_from lineage)
2. Execution completes with status complete
3. SSE events include stage events and SDK task events

Case Name: Degradation behavior when the LLM dependency is unavailable
Steps:
1. Cut network access to the LLM endpoint or configure an unreachable address
2. Submit an intent generation request
3. Observe the response and logs
Expected Result:
1. The API returns a clear error (e.g., 503/business error code) without a partial PSOP
2. Logs record the reason for the LLM call failure

Case Name: A2A-T four message types dual-transport consistency
Precondition: Python and Java sample agents both registered and discoverable by each other
Steps:
1. The same pair of agents sends Task-T tasks via both JSON-RPC and HTTP+REST transports
2. Trigger Negotiation-T negotiation and Notification-T event subscription
3. Verify that Authorization-T denies unauthorized operations
Expected Result:
1. Task state machines are consistent across both transports
2. Negotiation process states are aligned
3. Unauthorized operations are denied and logged
Notes: Cross-language SDK interoperability (python sdk ↔ java sdk)

Case Name: Broadband complaint handling multi-agent end-to-end scenario
Precondition: All core components deployed; customer service/billing/CDN/vendor fault sample agents ready
Steps:
1. Simulate a call center submitting a "no internet access" complaint intent
2. Observe the Orchestration Center workflow recall, agent retrieval, and A2A-T collaboration execution
3. Check the SSE event stream and execution results
Expected Result:
1. The workflow automatically recalls and correctly orchestrates the relevant agents
2. The agents collaborate to complete the diagnosis
3. The execution result contains the diagnosis conclusion and handling suggestions
Notes: Scenario package source: openan-demo mockagent scenarios
